note: Obeticholic acid went from rat cholestasis models to an ALP response in UDCA-inadequate PBC (accelerated approval 2016), but the confirmatory outcome trial COBALT showed no benefit and cirrhotic patients decompensated at labelled doses; EU authorisation was later withdrawn and US marketing is discontinued.
label: PBC (FXR agonists)

engagement.model: Rat liver FXR target genes (estrogen-cholestasis rat)
engagement.note: 6-ECDCA (obeticholic acid) induced Shp and Bsep and repressed Cyp7a1 in rat liver; bile-acid synthesis suppression was the engagement read-out.
engagement.short: OCA induced Shp/Bsep, repressed Cyp7a1 in rats
engagement.quote: In vivo administration of 6-ECDCA increased liver expression of Shp, bsep, multidrug resistance-associated protein-2, and multidrug resistance protein-2, whereas it reduced cyp7a1 and cyp8b1 and ntcp mRNA.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level reading. Pellicciari 2002 used the rat model first but its abstract gives no target-engagement read-out, so the engagement strip opens here.

engagement.model: Rat liver FXR target genes (estrogen-cholestasis rat)
engagement.note: In POISE, OCA 10 mg raised FGF-19 173% and lowered circulating cholic and chenodeoxycholic acid: the same FXR-FGF19-CYP7A1 axis the rat showed.
engagement.short: FGF-19 up 173%, bile acids down in PBC
engagement.quote: In Trial 1, administration of OCALIVA 10 mg once daily was associated with a 173% increase in concentrations of FGF-19, an FXR-inducible enterokine involved in bile acid homeostasis, from baseline to Month 12.
engagement.reason: FGF19 rose, bile acids fell in PBC
engagement.judgement: Label (section 12.2) gives the patient-side FGF-19/bile-acid data but makes no rodent comparison, and adds 'the clinical relevance of these findings is unknown'; I juxtaposed it with Fiorucci 2005. The rat read-out was hepatic Shp/Cyp7a1, the human read-out intestinal FGF19 and C4 (EMA EPAR p.46-47 shows dose-dependent FGF-19 rise and C4 fall in study 747-202), so the match is on direction of the same axis, not magnitude. Registry date is POISE NCT01473524 results-first-posted; the phase 2 NCT00550862 (FGF19 a secondary outcome) posted results 2012-01-23.

dose.note: Rat mg/kg doses were never scaled to a human target; the 5-10 mg clinical dose came from two phase 2 ALP dose-ranging trials (10-50 mg).
dose.short: Clinical dose set by phase 2, not rats
dose.quote: Dose selection for the phase III study was based on 2 phase II studies, 747-201 and 747-202.
dose.reason: Clinical dose set by phase 2 ALP
dose.judgement: Year is the first rat use (Pellicciari 2002, doi:10.1021/jm025529g); the EPAR (p.95) is cited because it documents that no model-derived exposure target was carried into the clinic. No published rat-to-human dose or occupancy comparison was found. Human hepatic-impairment PK (AUC 4x and 17x in Child-Pugh B/C) drove the weekly dosing, again without a model.

efficacy.note: 6-ECDCA (obeticholic acid) reversed cholestasis in rats; the regulatory package later added rat LCA-cholestasis, TAA-fibrosis and cirrhosis models. No PBC model exists.
efficacy.quote: Among them, 6alpha-ethyl-chenodeoxycholic acid (6-ECDCA) was shown to be a very potent and selective FXR agonist (EC(50) = 99 nM) and to be endowed with anticholeretic activity in an in vivo rat model of cholestasis.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level reading; the abstract says 'anticholeretic', quoted verbatim. Models filed per EMA EPAR p.20: rat acute cholestasis (LCA co-infusion), rat TAA fibrosis, rat TAA/BDL cirrhosis. Note the Mdr2-/- (Abcb4-/-) cholangiopathy mouse flagged OCA early: INT-747 'had no hepatoprotective effects' (Baghdasaryan 2011, doi:10.1002/hep.24537), but that model was not in the filing and is PSC-like, so it is not the 'best model' here.

efficacy.note: ALP fell 21-25% vs 3% on placebo in UDCA-inadequate PBC at 3 months; POISE (2016) confirmed 46-47% vs 10% composite response at 12 months.
efficacy.quote: Levels of ALP decreased 21%-25% on average from baseline in the OCA groups and 3% in the placebo group.
efficacy.magnitude_note: rat read-out was bile flow/bile-acid secretion, patient read-out serum ALP; not the same quantity
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level reading. The rat prediction (reduced cholestasis) matched the biochemical surrogate, which is what accelerated approval rested on (label: 'approved under accelerated approval based on a reduction in alkaline phosphatase'). POISE NCT01473524 (Nevens 2016, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1509840; results posted 2017-02-13) is the pivotal confirmation; registry date given is the earlier phase 2 NCT00550862.

efficacy.note: COBALT: death/transplant/decompensation composite 28.6% on OCA vs 28.9% on placebo (HR 1.01); the biochemical response did not become a disease response.
efficacy.quote: In the RCT, the primary endpoint occurred in 28.6% of OCA (n = 168) and 28.9% of placebo patients (n = 166; intent-to-treat analysis hazard ratio [HR] = 1.01, 95% confidence interval = 0.68-1.51)
efficacy.judgement: This is a call. The rat models predicted less cholestasis and fibrosis; patients got the biochemistry but not the outcome, so under the brief's efficacy question (did the disease respond the way the model said) the answer is no. Caveats: COBALT (NCT02308111, terminated) was confounded by functional unblinding and crossover to commercial OCA, and the authors' propensity-weighted external control favours OCA (HR 0.39); the rat models never carried an outcome endpoint, so one can read this as a surrogate failure rather than a model failure. Abstract-level reading; print year 2025 (Am J Gastroenterol 120:390-400), epub 2024-08-14. Tropifexor also lowered GGT 26-72% in UDCA-inadequate PBC (Schramm 2022, doi:10.1016/j.jhepr.2022.100544) with no outcome data; cilofexor/EDP-305 PBC results were not verified in this session.

safety.note: In TAA and bile-duct-ligated cirrhotic rats OCA lowered portal pressure, i.e. the cirrhosis models predicted benefit, not harm.
safety.short: Cirrhotic rats: OCA lowered portal pressure
safety.quote: Treatment with INT-747 in TAA and BDL reactivated the FXR downstream signaling pathway and decreased portal pressure by lowering total IHVR without deleterious systemic hypotension.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level reading. The EPAR (p.20) cites these cirrhosis models in the filing. Repeat-dose toxicology predates this but has no earlier public primary source, so the strip opens at the first published safety-relevant model use.

safety.note: EMA assessor: hepatobiliary target-organ toxicity in animals predicted the dose-limiting hepatic toxicity seen in PBC patients at 5x the 10 mg dose.
safety.quote: Thus, the main toxicity finding (hepatobiliary effects) in nonclinical species is predictive of toxicity in human populations at similar therapeutic margins.
safety.judgement: The EPAR (p.~29) states the comparison itself: reversible hepatobiliary toxicity in animals, and 'signs of toxicity occur in patients with PBC at doses that are 5-fold higher than the proposed maximum dose of 10 mg, and toxicity would not be expected at therapeutic doses.' The EMA review is not in the brief's enumerated source list (FDA review/label, DOI paper, registry) but is the EMA equivalent of an FDA review; flagging for the reviewer. Magnitude left at direction_only because I did not extract the animal NOAEL multiples. Registry date = phase 2 NCT00550862 (25-50 mg arms where the hepatic DLT appeared).

safety.note: Hepatic decompensation and death in cirrhotic PBC patients at the recommended dosage; FDA contraindicated OCA in decompensated cirrhosis and in compensated cirrhosis with portal hypertension.
safety.short: Decompensation in cirrhotics at labelled dose
safety.quote: cases of hepatic decompensation and failure have continued to be reported in patients with decompensated cirrhosis even when they received the recommended dosage.
safety.reason: Decompensation at labelled dose in cirrhotics
safety.judgement: Two model predictions failed in cirrhotic patients: the toxicology-based expectation that 'toxicity would not be expected at therapeutic doses' (EPAR 2016) and the cirrhotic-rat prediction of improved portal hypertension (Verbeke 2014). The 2018 boxed warning was an overdose story (Child-Pugh B/C patients dosed daily instead of weekly; AUC 4x and 17x), consistent with the animal margin and so not a contradiction; the 5/2021 revision is, because cases continued at the recommended dosage and the drug was contraindicated in decompensated cirrhosis and in compensated cirrhosis with portal hypertension. Text was read from the Feb-2022 revision (s008), whose Recent Major Changes block dates the boxed warning, contraindication and 5.1 to 5/2021; the 5/2021 label itself (207999s007lbl.pdf) was not opened. Postmarketing signal, so no registry date.
